data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Chris Power, currently carries a $1.6B post-money valuation after raising $1.37B to date. The valuation assessment draws from a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—spanning the same sector and stage, including Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Divergent ($2.3B Series E), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C).

Two valuation methods were triangulated. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, yields $2.4B. The peer-median method across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables produces $1.5B, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods reflect different assumptions: stage progression anchors to forward-looking capital structures, while peer medians capture current market positioning.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B (low) to $2.8B (high), with a median of $1.9B. This implies modest upside from the current $1.6B valuation under conservative scenarios, though the wide range reflects uncertainty in peer selection and stage-specific multipliers. Key variables driving outcomes include the timing and terms of next-round financing and relative operational performance versus peer benchmarks.
